summary:
A Hessen Landtag parliamentary inquiry documents that queer-hostile offences recorded by police rose from 33 in 2022 to 83 in 2023, and the same answer reports 135 in 2024 (+52 on the prior year, which the interior minister's reply calls alarming). The dossier flags an irreducible ambiguity: the increases may reflect a real deterioration in safety or a change in police classification practices under the newer BKA LSBTIQ reporting category. No Land-specific trans statute, ordinance or documented event-attack series was found for Hessen beyond this statistical finding; the police have run dedicated LSBTIQ liaison officers in every headquarters since 2010.

National score is 0.71. Hessen sits 0.02 below — the minimum deviation threshold — reflecting a concerning trend whose causality is unresolved. Compared to Bayern (0.67), Hessen lacks any equivalent legislative hostility (no SBGG-initiative participation, no language ban); compared to Berlin (0.73), the statistical signal is the only differentiator and it is caveated. The small deviation treats the trend as a mild negative climate indicator pending confirmation.

sources.summary: Hessen Landtag small inquiry and Interior Minister answer (April 2025): police-registered queer-hostile offences in Hessen rose from 33 (2022) to 83 (2023) and to 135 (2024, +52 year-on-year — described as alarming); notes LSBTIQ* liaison officers established in all police headquarters since 2010 and a framework concept governing them.

Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) situation report on the security of LSBTIQ* people in Germany, published with the Interior Ministry: a multi-year rise in police-registered queer-hostile offences and the new federal reporting category that makes Land-by-Land comparison possible; classification changes can inflate Land counts, so cross-Land numbers need caution.

tangentialFactors: The recorded rise covers queer-hostile crime generally — the KPMD category combines hostility to sexual orientation and to gender-related diversity — so the trend is a general negative-climate signal rather than a trans-specific series.
